procedure: EA-NEGONT-02 v0.7 §3.4 D/R/O (working; not frozen). Admission by reading: D, a claim on what political economy is, does, lacks, its history, its questions or its critique; R, a relation between political economy and an archive object (the Semantic Economy, ontological economy, meaning feudalism, Operative Semiotics, the archive's journals and domains, the bridge packet); O, an archive category applied to political economy (semiotic strike, Phase X, Layer 3, boundary law, coherence value, means of denotation). Naming political economy is not enough; 'the political economy of X' used as a lens on another object is not a claim on the entity. Machine compositions quoted in deposits are reception evidence and are not admitted. Volume is never a ground of removal; S4 redundancy only. The hop (H) was run for one edge only (#1634 → #1666, named in the task).

The archive's packet whose primary entity is political economy. O: semantic physics stratification places the political economy of meaning at Layer 3, with Marxian operators.

R: the archive's suppression findings and its political economy as one subject.

Defining paper of ontological economy. D/O: 'the political economy of machine-mediated existence'; its questions stated as political-economic; classical political economy's means of production against means of identification; the succession factory → platform → AI. Limits: mediation not illegitimate; censorship established only by evidence.

Disambiguation packet for the Semantic Economy (panel entity, kept distinct): R: the framework defined as 'the political economy of meaning' with seven linked distinctions; inverted-fan path from political economy; dating 'from December 2025'. Limit: claims the accounting system, never the phrase.

Admitted at the hop (H), one citation hop back from #1634 (it extends #1634, #939, #1616); term-absent for 'political economy', so the string pass could not find it. R: applies #1634's externality and bill to flattening: privately profitable, socially negative, who holds the bag. Hypotheses carried as hypotheses; falsifiers and limits extracted.

not_admitted.reason: Citations, reference lists, registry rows and cross-references to works whose titles contain 'political economy' (#234's title, Marx's Capital and Grundrisse, Stiegler, Rubin, Egan and others): no claim on political economy of their own.

S4 redundancy: navigation maps, registries, announcements, later editions and disambiguations repeating a line already carried from an admitted instance ('Political economy of meaning' for the Semantic Economy, #205/#704; 'meaning as political economy', #364; Transactions' scope, #516; ASW chapter 7, #499; the primer, #288; the semiotic strike, #950; the Marx room, #577; Marx's liquidated method, #501; the Constitution, #1127; diversity contraction, #779; semantic exhaustion as a construct of the political economy of meaning, #704/#1644 lineage). Instances stay in the provenance graph under the lineage.
Machine compositions quoted in deposits (AI Overview, AI Mode, ChatGPT traversals and captures) and conversational transcript lines: reception evidence, not admitted as archive claims.

'The political economy of X' used as a lens or heading on another object (time and aspect, the like button, ad placement, proxy governance, scholarly labor, variance preservation, sacred text, interface labor), or keyword and self-positioning lists: no claim on what political economy is, does, lacks or how it stands to the archive.

observations: Field frame checked against: the field (Wikipedia, Harvard, Britannica, UE, EBSCO) defines political economy as the interdisciplinary study of the mutual influence of politics and economics, traces it from 16th-century moral philosophy and Smith/Ricardo/Marx to its separation from economics after Marshall (1890), and lists modern topics, subfields (comparative, international) and schools. The archive mostly does not dispute that frame: #727 restates it (definition, subfields, 'do not reduce to economics or partisan politics') and then adds a thesis on its ground (meaning) and a succession (factory → platform → AI → meaning, #1634, #499, #133, #514).

The archive's strongest claim on the entity is #727's 'Political economy has always already been semantic economy', with its stated limit (not 'everything is language') and its own risk (disembodiment, §3.7). #726 states that the packet did not try to own the field term; #727's header states its indexing function. These are carried at their grade (interpretation; self-description).

Corrective line: #533 contests a redefinition of political economy that removes authority, allocation and scarcity; the field's Harvard and EBSCO definitions are neutral on this and are not targets of #533.

Critique-of-political-economy line (#501, #577, #950, #171, #1631, #18, #533): Kritik as analysis of conditions, value-form as critique of categories (attributed to the Neue Marx-Lektüre), the labor/labor-power distinction, immanent critique, a textual finding in Capital 1867. The field names Marx (B1, B5) and the Marxian critique of capital (B1 F22) without this line.

Dating is stated differently within the archive and is carried as such: #437 dates the Semantic Political Economy series 29–30 December 2024; #704 gives first_use 2025-01; #205 (2026-01-01) gives '(2025)'; #1644 gives 'developed by Lee Sharks from December 2025'. No reading here resolves it.

Distinct from the panel entity semantic-economy: claims whose subject is the Semantic Economy are admitted only where they state its relation to political economy (R), never as claims about political economy itself.
#1666 is term-absent and enters only through the hop from #1634; the hop was run for that one edge, named in the task, and not exhaustively.
